## What to build

Keep package-generated dtplyr contextual-share membership independent of an unrelated `%in%` root binding, retaining ADR 0010/0017 share values and caller expression lookup.

## Reproduction

Confirmed independently on main `1b3e8df656f0523ef21f85298f6db5c865e1e12a`, macOS arm64, R 4.6.1, dplyr 1.2.1, dtplyr 1.3.3, data.table 1.18.6.1, rlang 1.3.0. The bounded reproduction asserted the observed failures and controls and exited 0; no relevant guards were skipped.

```r
pkgload::load_all()
root <- new.env(parent = globalenv())
root$source <- data.frame(g = c("b", "a", NA_character_), x = 1:3)
input <- evalq(dtplyr::lazy_dt(source), root)
query <- summarize_with_margins(input, total = sum(x),
  p = share_of_total(total), .grouping = rollup(g), .sort = "last")
dplyr::collect(query) # a/b/NA/Total; p = 2/6, 1/6, 3/6, 1
root$`%in%` <- function(...) stop("caller membership helper ran")
dplyr::collect(query) # Error: caller membership helper ran
dplyr::collect(input) # original input; no callback
rm(list = "%in%", envir = root)
dplyr::collect(query) # expected result restored
```

Parent shares reproduce the same failure. Source bytes remain unchanged. A root binding present before construction also fails at collection. Construction remains lazy.

## Cause and scope

`apply_share_ratios()` in `R/share.R` generates an unqualified `%in%` test for own-denominator Grouping set identifiers. Audit other generated share membership expressions too. This differs from the final ordering expressions repaired by #1176/#1197, Margin-label helpers (#1143), nesting display extraction (#1089), and special-measure lexical alias rewriting (#1033/#1186). Preserve caller-written helper lookup, other backend translations, source immutability and lazy boundaries.

## Duplicate search

All-state issue/PR queries: `share "%in%"`, `share helper binding`, `share membership caller`, `dtplyr share lexical`, `dtplyr share caller`, `dtplyr membership`; also all-state `dtplyr` lists filtered for caller/helper/lexical/binding/membership. Full bodies/comments of #1176, #1143, #1089, #1033 and #1186 and the #1197 record were examined. No duplicate or matching repair found.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Parent/Total ratios and own-denominator ones remain correct under preexisting and late root `%in%` bindings.
- [ ] Package-generated membership never invokes those callbacks; cover counting and raising callbacks and relevant denominator-selection paths.
- [ ] Preserve ordinary caller expression lookup, source bytes, visible names, local/native controls and lazy construction.
- [ ] Add public-seam tests under the optional-backend policy.

## Blocked by

None. Separate defect found during bounded checking for PR #1192; that PR does not repair it.
title: [P2] Isolate dtplyr contextual-share membership from caller bindings

body:
## What to build

Keep the package-generated Grouping set identifier repetition independent of a dtplyr root environment binding for rep. An empty, zero-column input must remain empty when expansion attaches .id.

## Reproduction

Confirmed on current main 7f0aecaf6a71a103315f25a56badf5835475489c and independently on the #1143 submission e02394cfc91a16a95486a038057f21fd1d3fb5be. R 4.6.1, dplyr 1.2.1, dtplyr 1.3.3, data.table 1.18.6.1 on macOS arm64; provisioned library, no dependency changes. Both minimal reproductions completed with exit 0; no tests or optional-backend guards were skipped.

```r
pkgload::load_all()
root <- new.env(parent = globalenv())
root$source <- data.table::data.table()
input <- evalq(dtplyr::lazy_dt(source), root)
query <- expand_with_margins(input, .grouping = grouping_set(), .id = "set")
dplyr::collect(query) # 0 rows, integer set column
root$rep <- function(...) 999L
dplyr::collect(query) # 1 fabricated row, set = 999L
dplyr::collect(input) # still 0 rows, 0 columns
```

Expected: the already-built expansion remains empty, and generated identifier attachment does not invoke the caller rep. Observed: late rebinding alone invents a row with an invalid Grouping set identifier. Native collection remains empty.

## Contract and cause

The source-row cardinality and identifier-attachment contract is established by #184 and its repair #201. add_grouping_set_id() in R/grouping-adapter-union.R generates unqualified rep(id, dplyr::n()) when count_branch_rows is true. dtplyr defers that generated call to the input root environment. This expression is distinct from the Margin-label expressions repaired for #1143, and a zero-column input has no Margin dimension or label transformation.

Do not change the documented inability of data.table to represent positive rows with zero columns, and preserve ordinary lexical lookup of caller-written expressions and the lazy expansion boundary.

## Duplicate search

All-state issue searches: dtplyr rep; "zero-column" identifier; dtplyr "caller" "identifier"; "rep" "zero-column". All-state PR searches: dtplyr rep; "zero-column" "identifier"; "rep" "caller" "identifier". Read full bodies/comments for #184 and #201, plus #1143. #184/#201 fixed literal identifier recycling but did not isolate the later generated rep expression. #1143 concerns Margin-label helpers, not this independent zero-column identifier expression. No matching open repair or duplicate found.

## Acceptance criteria

- Empty zero-column dtplyr expansion with .id remains empty under root rep bindings, including late rebinding after construction.
- Both nesting verbs preserve their documented empty-input results through the shared identifier path.
- Native collection controls, source immutability and lazy/eager collection boundaries are preserved.
- Explicitly caller-written rep calls retain ordinary lexical lookup.
title: [P2] Isolate zero-column dtplyr identifier repetition from caller bindings

body:
## What to build

Acquire typed metadata from the visible schema of a supported derived dtplyr input without revalidating source columns that an upstream selection has already removed.

## Evidence and reproduction

Investigated on main snapshot `4c63bb917ed7ed31ff6aadf060a5eae7a32cd004` with R 4.6.1, data.table 1.18.6.1, dtplyr 1.3.3, and dplyr 1.2.1. This ticket records a confirmed bug-hunt finding; no repair was implemented during the investigation.

Create a data.table with a character column renamed to `..1`, `..2`, or `...`, plus an integer value column and logical flag column. Build an immutable lazy input and select only value and flag. Ordinary collection succeeds with those safe visible names. Name-only Grouping-plan inspection also succeeds. Typed inspection using an integer or logical predicate, and each of the four Margin verbs over a rollup of value with flag as fixed key, instead fail with `tibble_error_column_names_cannot_be_dot_dot` naming the discarded source column.

The 126-case audit covered three names, zero/one/three rows, dropping versus renaming away the source column, and seven public operations. All 54 dropped-source typed-inspection/Margin-operation cases failed; all nine name-only inspection cases and all 63 rename-away controls passed. Ordinary collected/local controls passed and source mutation was not observed. The metadata path converted the root to a validated tibble before applying the derived projection, reintroducing a name absent from the requested input.

These names have R/tibble restrictions as well as data.table's double-dot syntax; the request does not expand support for visible unsupported names. It concerns a safe derived input. #947 concerned retained `.SD` metadata, #968 generated identifiers, and #1002 admitted signed dot-dot column reads; none covered discarded root columns.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Typed dimension/fixed-key inspection of the safely projected input agrees with inspection of its ordinary collected result.
- [ ] Summary, expansion, and both nesting verbs work on that input and agree with local results, including empty inputs.
- [ ] Projection and rename-away controls retain accurate types and source isolation. Tests distinguish discarded names from genuinely unsupported visible schemas.
- [ ] Acquire metadata without running row predicates or reading source data beyond the existing schema-only policy, and retain existing special-name metadata protections.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

## Investigation evidence

[PR #1052](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/pull/1052) records the dated audit, executable reproductions, successful controls, expected failing repair assertions, and version/scope limits.
title: [P2] Ignore discarded dot-dot source names when acquiring dtplyr metadata

## Summary

```text
locally resolved fixed keys and dimension prefix
  -> Nest .key and row-wise .rows admission
  -> once keys and dimensions are complete: summary and Margin label names
  -> typed metadata and remaining type-dependent validation
```

Closes #1307. Closes #1308.

## Evidence

- **Before:** At `770d9203`, both Nest verbs return an unsafe-dtplyr metadata refusal before a known `.key` conflict; DuckDB sends one `selection_proxy` statement before rejecting an unknown Margin label name.
  **After:** Known Nest conflicts and Margin label names receive their existing diagnostics before metadata. DuckDB name errors send zero statements; typed selections retain their normal metadata path.
- Verification: [Review-ready full for final SHA `611da2a8`](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/pull/1339#issuecomment-6653652501), including 240 test files and 0 ERROR / WARNING / NOTE.
- Review: [Standards and Spec findings and dispositions](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/pull/1339#issuecomment-6652875249).

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

The validation-order change can be reverted.

**Blast Radius:** validation

Margin verbs reject locally decidable output and label names earlier. Type-dependent selection, semantic label validation and supported `.rows` payload/list-column roles retain their existing paths.
title: Reject locally known Nest and Margin label names before metadata


title: Fix Margin summary evaluation and public-name boundaries

body:
## Parent

[Restore Margin-operation correctness at grouping and backend boundaries](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/issues/599) (#599).

## What to build

Apply Mutable-step refusal and inspection isolation to every contributing dtplyr input. A join with a mutable source in its second internal input lost a source column before collection; inspection did the same. When both inputs were mutable, inspection still failed to isolate the second source even though detection could see the first.

Margin execution must refuse before reads or writes. Inspection remains available without changing caller tables. Extend #451 and ADR 0029 independently of upstream report #468. Any shared input-graph traversal preparation is part of this ticket, used consistently for both detection and isolation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every Margin verb refuses a derivation with any mutable root, using the existing Package condition and immutable-input remediation.
- [ ] Public tests cover joins/unions with the mutable source in either position, both sources mutable, and nested derivations.
- [ ] Refusal leaves every source unchanged in names, rows, values, and types, with no preceding backend data read.
- [ ] inspect_grouping accepts the same inputs, including type-based selections, without evaluating any mutable branch against an unisolated source.
- [ ] Single-source and all-immutable controls preserve their successful results; source state is checked immediately after uncollected calls and inspection.
- [ ] No full-input copying or implicit materialization is used to allow execution. Version checks, grammar-error precedence, and the policy for unavailable private backend fields remain intact.
- [ ] ADR 0029 and Mutable step terminology are amended where a single-parent description is false. Tests require only the dtplyr backend, and the Review-ready check passes before review.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).
title: Protect every input of a dtplyr Mutable-step graph

body:
## Problem Statement

Running several marginplyr worktrees concurrently can start several four-worker test suites on the same Mac and make it unresponsive. Review-ready has also accumulated routing, evidence reuse, infrastructure self-tests, recovery, and delivery machinery whose complexity is disproportionate to the original coordination problem. Infrastructure self-tests can take longer than the package tests they precede.

The maintainer wants a small, understandable local workflow: preserve useful checks and progress reporting, serialize the expensive package check, and avoid waiting for that slot merely to discover a lint error. Light documentation changes must still receive the five mandatory source/environment checks. The AI should decide whether the expensive local package check is necessary by reasoning about the change, rather than introducing another automatic classifier.

The installed legacy CLI and instructions directing agents to use it must eventually be retired together. Local check by-products must have one simple retention policy instead of accumulating indefinitely.

## Solution

Use one repository-owned R entry with two explicit execution forms. Both run the same five mandatory checks against a pinned committed revision. The AI decides and records whether local package build/check is needed. A five-check-only invocation ends after those checks without requesting the shared slot. A heavy invocation requests the slot only after those checks pass, then automatically starts package build and the complete source-tarball check when admitted.

One heavy Review-ready check may run at a time across this user's marginplyr clones and worktrees on the Mac; its testthat suite uses four workers. Keep ordinary polling of the same execution handle, existing progress reporting, the existing investigation loop, and the existing bounded additional focused-test policy. Remove automatic crash retries, routine local infrastructure self-tests, automatic AI stop/resume messages, stage reuse, and custom coordination services. Retained infrastructure tests run in CI on every relevant PR.

Keep all runner-managed artifacts for an invocation together in one ignored directory inside its submitting worktree, outside Git's administrative directory. Seven days after the recorded UTC start time, that directory becomes eligible for deletion on the next invocation in the same worktree. Never delete active data.

## User Stories

1. As a maintainer, I want one repository-owned R entry, so that the checked-out code supplies the check implementation without synchronizing an installed launcher.
2. As a maintainer using several worktrees, I want expensive Review-ready checks serialized across them, so that their four-worker suites do not all overload my Mac at once.
3. As a maintainer using separate clones, I want the same shared slot to apply across clones, so that another clone cannot accidentally bypass the load limit.
4. As a developer, I want four testthat workers within the admitted package check, so that a single check retains its existing useful parallelism.
5. As an agent, I want checks to use the submitted committed revision even after waiting, so that I can identify exactly what the result establishes.
6. As a reviewer, I want the result to name the submitted SHA, so that later edits cannot be presented as already checked.
7. As an agent making a light documentation change, I want all five mandatory checks to run, so that omitting the expensive package check does not omit basic verification.
8. As a maintainer, I want the AI to judge whether local package build/check is necessary from the diff and its effects, so that another path-based classifier is unnecessary.
9. As a reviewer, I want the reason for omitting local package build/check recorded, so that the AI's judgment is reviewable.
10. As an agent, I want an explicit five-check-only execution form, so that a justified omission does not require waiting for the heavy slot.
11. As a reviewer, I want a five-check-only result distinguished from a full package-check pass, so that the result cannot overstate what ran.
12. As a developer, I want test dependency declarations checked mechanically, so that this validation does not depend on AI recollection.
13. As a developer, I want required optional test dependencies and their versions checked mechanically, so that a green suite cannot merely reflect avoidable skips.
14. As a developer, I want package spelling checked before joining the heavy-check wait, so that spelling failures are found promptly.
15. As a developer, I want jarl checked before joining the heavy-check wait, so that a lint failure does not waste a long admission wait.
16. As a developer, I want lintr to run with the package loaded before joining the heavy-check wait, so that internal symbols are resolved correctly and lint failures are found promptly.
17. As an agent, I want a failed mandatory check to end the invocation, so that build/check does not proceed after a known failure.
18. As a maintainer, I want fixes made and committed explicitly before a new invocation, so that the runner does not silently edit code or retry against an unclear revision.
19. As an agent waiting for capacity, I want the command to start automatically when the slot becomes available, so that no admission acknowledgment is needed.
20. As an agent, I want to retain and poll the same execution handle through terminal completion, so that I do not launch duplicate checks or infer success from partial output.
21. As a maintainer, I want no queued AI resumption messages, so that a stale message cannot restart a conversation after its work is already complete.
22. As an agent, I want the existing meaningful investigation loop retained while waiting or checking, so that I can use that time to examine the submitted change.
23. As an agent, I want the existing bounded focused-test allowance retained, so that I can test a concrete hypothesis without launching another full suite.
24. As a maintainer, I want the distinction between the shared heavy slot and extra focused tests documented, so that four workers is not mistaken for an account-wide process cap.
25. As an observer, I want existing elapsed-time, completed-file, percentage, and last-file progress reporting preserved, so that a long package check remains understandable.
26. As a developer, I want native worker startup and failure diagnostics visible, so that failures before or after reporter completion are not hidden.
27. As a reviewer, I want the terminal check result to determine the verdict, so that progress output is never mistaken for success.
28. As a maintainer, I want check failures to stop without an automatic native-crash retry, so that the runner avoids a special retry classification subsystem.
29. As an agent, I want ordinary cancellation to stop owned child work before releasing capacity, so that the next admitted check does not overlap normally cancelled work.
30. As an agent, I want cancellation during admission waiting to prevent later automatic start, so that a cancelled request stays cancelled.
31. As a maintainer, I want abrupt-termination cleanup to use existing libraries with explicit limits, so that strict crash recovery does not recreate a custom supervision platform.
32. As a developer making routine package changes, I want infrastructure regression suites excluded from the normal local command, so that those suites do not dominate every check.
33. As a maintainer, I want retained infrastructure tests executed in CI on every relevant PR, so that removing them from routine local orchestration does not leave them untested.
34. As a maintainer, I want actual CI invocations for retained progress and runner tests, so that registering a test is not mistaken for executing it.
35. As a maintainer, I want all runner-managed source copies, archives, check outputs, caches, logs, and results grouped per invocation, so that cleanup is understandable.
36. As a maintainer, I want output storage inside the worktree but outside Git's administrative directory, so that artifacts have an ordinary local location without entering Git or the source package.
37. As a maintainer, I want one seven-day lifetime for all artifacts and outcomes, so that separate success, failure, cache, and log retention rules are unnecessary.
38. As a maintainer, I want retention measured from one recorded UTC start time, so that log updates and missing finish records do not change the deadline.
39. As a maintainer, I want expired data deleted on a later invocation in the same worktree, so that no background cleanup service is required.
40. As a maintainer, I want cleanup restricted to the current worktree and inactive owned data, so that a check cannot sweep another worktree or delete live work.
41. As a maintainer, I want unrelated installed tools, libraries, caches, research files, and OS reports left alone, so that retention cleanup stays within its ownership boundary.
42. As a maintainer who is the only legacy CLI user, I want a one-time retirement and instruction update, so that permanent compatibility machinery is unnecessary.
43. As a maintainer, I want old worktrees and their existing AI sessions excluded from migration, so that adoption does not become a fleet-upgrade exercise.
44. As a maintainer, I want obsolete checker-owned state removed only after old work has stopped, so that retirement does not interrupt live work or keep unneeded history forever.
45. As an implementer, I want the old ADRs and operational guidance reconciled with this specification, so that future agents do not receive contradictory entry-point, reuse, or retention instructions.

## Implementation Decisions

1. **Entry and scope.** Keep a repository-tracked R command as the interface. Implement a small orchestration boundary around existing check, progress, process, and locking facilities. Prefer existing focused R libraries and base R over a new admission service, custom queue manager, or general recovery framework.
2. **Two explicit execution forms.** Support the five mandatory checks alone and the same checks followed by heavy package verification. The AI explicitly supplies the chosen scope and records its reasoning. Exact option spelling is an implementation detail. This is not a new automatically inferred classification system.
3. **AI decision boundary.** The AI examines the submitted diff and its effects to decide whether local package build/check is required. Package-affecting changes require it. Light documentation, prose, or research changes may omit it when their effects justify omission. Neither a directory name, extension, nor exclusion from the source package alone proves that omission is justified. The AI may omit only the heavy portion, never the mandatory five-check baseline.
4. **Pinned input.** Check one clean committed revision, pinned at invocation, through a disposable committed-source copy. All preflight and heavy checks use that revision. Waiting does not switch to a later HEAD, and an earlier result does not certify later changes. Do not introduce cross-run stage reuse or a branch's first-success requirement.
5. **Mandatory checks.** A successful invocation requires the mechanical test dependency-declaration scan, required optional test Suggests presence/version check, package spelling, jarl, and package-aware lintr. Load the package before lintr so namespace-dependent symbol resolution works. Preserve these existing checks rather than substituting AI judgment for their execution.
6. **Pre-admission failure.** Run the five checks before requesting the heavy slot. A failure ends that invocation without joining admission waiting or starting build/check. The agent corrects the issue, commits the correction, and starts a new invocation. The command does not edit code or silently retry failed checks.
7. **Five-check-only completion.** After the five checks succeed, report their outcome, submitted SHA, heavy-check omission, and the agent's reason, then exit without requesting the heavy slot. Do not report this as a full package-check pass. The same artifact and retention policy applies to this form.
8. **Heavy-check admission.** Use one stable OS-backed advisory lock for this user's marginplyr clones/worktrees on the Mac. After successful preflight, wait inside the command and start automatically when admitted. Do not add an agent-ready handshake. Keep the same invocation and execution identity through waiting, checking, cleanup, and terminal completion.
9. **Heavy-check contents.** Under that slot, build a source tarball and run the existing as-CRAN package-check contents, including examples, vignette rebuilding, the complete test suite, and snapshots once, with four testthat workers and without coverage measurement. Preserve the existing required-Suggests enforcement and local/offline check environment. Do not copy unrelated complexity merely because it exists in an older runner.
10. **Check outcomes.** ERROR, WARNING, nonzero process exit, and timeout fail the invocation. Print every NOTE; classifications outside the existing shared policy need a written disposition before review readiness. Retain the ordinary result and logs. Remove the native-rendering-crash recognizer, automatic retry, retry eligibility rules, and passed-after-retry outcome.
11. **Progress.** Preserve existing custom test progress: elapsed time, completed files versus total, percentage, last completed file, native worker-count announcement, and worker startup/exit/teardown diagnostics. Keep observing diagnostics through terminal completion, including failures before reporter startup or after reporter completion. Percentages describe file completion, not passing tests or an estimate of remaining time. Progress is observational; only the terminal result determines the verdict.
12. **AI observation.** Retain ordinary polling of the same execution handle until its terminal result. Do not infer completion from elapsed time, partial logs, or process absence, and do not silently replace a lost invocation. Avoid repeated idle narration. Do not implement AI stop/resume coordination or completion-message queues; zero-token waiting is not a guarantee of this design.
13. **Investigation policy retained.** Preserve the existing same-agent hypothesis, investigation, evidence, and disposition loop while waiting or checking. Investigate meaningful hypotheses; once they are exhausted, checkpoint and wait on the original invocation. Retaining the loop does not require endless activity or repeated waiting messages.
14. **Focused-test policy retained.** Each submitting worktree may have at most one additional focused-test or reproduction execution at a time, with testthat parallelism disabled. Select the target explicitly, inspect its helpers and owned child work, and use a separate execution handle. Do not reconstruct a full suite through successive selections. Stop and collect that work before the next focused execution and when handling the Review-ready terminal transition.
15. **Concurrency boundary.** The shared slot covers the heavy Review-ready package check, not all R processes. Additional permitted focused tests may overlap across worktrees; there is no aggregate account-wide cap for them. Five worktrees can add five nonparallel focused-test executions alongside the four-worker package check. Do not introduce another scheduler to change that explicitly retained policy.
16. **Ordinary cancellation.** Stop the invocation's owned children and confirm their exit before releasing heavy-check capacity. A cancelled waiter must not later start checking. Retain available logs and report cancellation through the original handle.
17. **Abrupt termination.** Use existing process-library cleanup facilities when the R process itself is terminated abruptly. The maintainer accepts that a subsequent check may begin before all descendants stop. Do not recreate strict crash-time exclusion, a custom watchdog, or a durable recovery ledger. Verify actual library behavior on the target Mac instead of claiming normal R cleanup always runs after forced termination.
18. **Infrastructure verification.** Exclude infrastructure regression suites and real site/README regeneration verification from the routine local orchestration. Do not force an initial infrastructure self-test solely because a branch has no prior result. Keep appropriate change-specific development verification and CI. Run retained infrastructure tests on every relevant PR without adding change-path conditions for this simplification, and explicitly wire every retained runner/progress regression suite into CI. Remove suites for deleted machinery rather than preserving their old coverage counts.
19. **Artifacts.** Group all substantial runner-owned data per invocation in a dedicated output directory at the submitting worktree root, outside Git's administrative directory. This includes committed-source copies and archives, built tarballs, check/install work, supported child temporary/cache outputs, progress data, logs, and results. Exclude this output root from both Git tracking and R source builds. Use supported child environment settings to keep owned temporary/cache data under the run directory without recreating an isolation capability registry.
20. **Retention.** Record one UTC start timestamp when creating the run directory. Seven days means seven consecutive 24-hour periods from that recorded timestamp for all outcomes and artifact types. Reading or updating files does not renew it; a missing finish record does not require a different clock. On a subsequent invocation, remove eligible inactive run directories as a unit, only in the current worktree. Use a small existing OS-backed liveness guard, skip active or safety-undetermined data, and report cleanup problems rather than deleting uncertain data.
21. **Retention limits and exclusions.** Seven days is deletion eligibility, not a maximum on-disk age: an unused worktree is not swept by invocations elsewhere. Do not promise to preserve logs after worktree deletion. Stable shared-lock targets are operating primitives, not retained run history; do not expire or recreate them while owners or waiters may exist. Installed developer packages/tools, unrelated shared caches, tracked research, Codex history, and OS-owned crash reports are outside routine cleanup scope.
22. **One-time retirement.** After existing old checks finish or are cancelled and their work stops, adopt the simplified R entry, uninstall the legacy CLI, remove obsolete delivery/coordination machinery, and update repository plus user-wide Codex/Claude instructions together. Clean up obsolete checker-owned state and diagnostics after shutdown. Old worktrees and already-running sessions are explicitly outside migration scope: do not inventory, update, or provide a compatibility launcher for them.
23. **Documentation reconciliation.** Amend or supersede conflicting operational guidance and ADR decisions as part of eventual implementation and rollout. Preserve the useful repository-owned-entry decision while removing requirements for stage reuse, authenticated evidence, strict recovery, and migration of old worktrees that conflict with this approved simplification. Retain decision history without retaining the retired runtime machinery.

## Testing Decisions

- **Primary seam:** reuse the already-discussed repository R command/process boundary. Observe its exit/result, streamed output, owned child behavior, lock contention, and retained files. Prefer this highest existing seam over adding test-only service APIs or separately testing each orchestration helper.
- **Prior art:** existing disposable-package progress fixtures and runner process-contract fixtures already exercise real subprocesses, passing/failing tests, worker startup/exit/teardown failures, and process/lock boundaries. Reuse the applicable parts and retire tests for removed protocols. Registration consistency is not evidence that a fixture actually executes.
- **Good tests establish external behavior:** use tiny disposable repositories/packages and isolated fixture state to prove the requested workflow. Do not snapshot internal function layout, reproduce the implementation in assertions, or require the production package suite for every fixture case.
- **Mandatory baseline and scope:** prove that a light documentation-only invocation still executes all five checks, reports the AI-supplied heavy-check omission and reason, and never requests the heavy slot. Prove that heavy requests execute the same baseline first. A failed preflight must return failure without waiting for capacity or starting build/check.
- **Pinned revision:** submit one committed revision, hold capacity elsewhere, make later changes, and prove that the admitted check and its result still identify and use the submitted revision. An omitted heavy check must never be represented as a full package-check pass.
- **Real shared exclusion:** launch invocations from distinct worktrees and separate clones, prove at most one heavy check is admitted, then prove a waiter starts automatically when the slot is released. Preserve real four-worker behavior within the admitted package check. Do not assert a machine-wide four-process cap that contradicts the retained focused-test allowance.
- **Check execution and failure:** exercise successful and failing package-check fixtures, including preflight errors, check warnings/errors, nonzero exits, and timeout reporting. Preserve ordinary NOTE handling. Prove a supported native rendering failure ends once without an automatic retry or a passed-after-retry result.
- **Progress:** exercise real passing and failing disposable packages, file-completion reporting, actual worker-count announcements, startup failure, unexpected exit, and teardown failure. Prove diagnostics remain visible before progress events and after reporter completion, and that progress completion cannot override a failing terminal result.
- **Cancellation:** exercise a waiting cancellation that never subsequently starts, and an ordinary running cancellation with owned child work that stops before the slot becomes available. Exercise the available abrupt-parent cleanup on the actual Mac and document its accepted limits rather than asserting strict crash-time exclusion.
- **Artifacts and expiry:** demonstrate owned output confinement and exclusion from Git/source builds. Cover just-before/at/after the seven-day threshold from the recorded UTC start time, modified logs not extending retention, a killed run without a finish record, active/uncertain runs being protected, and another worktree's data remaining untouched. Verify success and failure use the same policy and deletion removes an eligible run as a unit.
- **Routine versus infrastructure checks:** prove a normal local invocation does not launch infrastructure regression suites, including on a branch without prior check history. Ensure every retained infrastructure suite has an actual every-PR CI invocation; specifically retain coverage for the preserved progress functionality. Ordinary package tests may use the reporter without running its regression suite.
- **Retirement acceptance:** verify the installed legacy entry and obsolete live machinery are removed at cutover, current shared instructions name the new entry, unrelated user data is untouched, and no old-worktree inventory or migration is required. Reconcile ADR and operational guidance conflicts before claiming rollout complete.
- **Execution policy:** infrastructure integration fixtures run in their CI/change-specific context, not as another prerequisite of every routine local invocation. One-time adoption evidence must cover the actual Mac and real execution handles. This specification task does not execute those checks.

## Out of Scope

- Implementing, deploying, uninstalling, or migrating anything in the current specification-writing session.
- Automatic three/four-way change classification, cross-run or cross-worktree stage reuse, authenticated evidence stores, key rotation, or a branch-baseline success requirement.
- A custom admission server, queue manager, watchdog, general recovery platform, strict forced-termination exclusion, or a scheduler for every R command.
- Automatic AI stopping/resumption, queued completion messages, or a zero-token waiting guarantee.
- Automatic native-crash retries or permanent legacy compatibility code.
- Migration, inspection, or individual instruction refresh of old worktrees and their existing AI sessions.
- Scheduled cleanup, sweeping other worktrees, distinct artifact lifetimes, permanent result storage, and cleanup of unrelated user/tool/OS data.
- Coverage measurement inside routine Review-ready, replacing the release matrix, or redesigning unrelated CI and release checks.

## Further Notes

- This is the consolidated specification for existing issue #1114, following the maintainer's 2026-11-02 design reset. Earlier interview proposals are historical where they conflict with this specification. Publishing this spec and marking it ready for an agent does not start implementation or local migration in this session.
- The agreed output layout is `<worktree-root>/.review-ready/runs/<run-id>/`, explicitly outside `.git`. The directory must be ignored by both Git and R builds during implementation.
- The retained six verification contents were established from historical commit `b5f851a25b227eb511127b4fef19d60817bbbc71`, immediately before shared admission was introduced. Reuse those verification contents, not the entire historical runner implementation.
- #1117 merged an earlier R bootstrap, but merge alone did not establish local cutover. Current operational instructions remain in force until the separately performed implementation/migration reconciles them.
- This target intentionally contradicts parts of accepted ADR 0038 and ADR 0039: reusable authenticated evidence, strict recovery, temporary-work cleanup before the common retention deadline, and compulsory old-worktree migration are not retained. Their accepted status must be reconciled explicitly during implementation; do not silently treat the old documents as already updated.
- The existing CI audit found a gate-contract invocation, a runner-process fixture invocation, and a renderer fixture invocation, but no direct workflow invocation for the dedicated progress fixture. CI rewiring must follow the simplified retained implementation. Required-status branch protection was not verified; do not claim these checks are already required merge statuses.
- A prior Codex notification experiment is not part of this target. Do not carry its probe, callback, or queued-message behavior into the implementation.
title: Simplify Review-ready with a repository-owned R runner and one shared heavy-check slot

body:
## Parent

Part of #23.

## What to build

Execute the final evidence-based release audit after all implementation, documentation, metadata, architecture, and CI tickets are complete. The ticket remains open until fresh Standards, Spec, and Docs & Tests reviews have no unresolved findings and CRAN-oriented checks satisfy the agreed gate. This ticket establishes readiness; it does not upload the package to CRAN.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Documentation is regenerated from the final source and the worktree contains no unexplained generated drift.
- [ ] Linting, the complete test suite, examples, vignettes, spelling, source-package build, and CRAN-oriented checks all run against the final state.
- [ ] Release, devel, and oldrel source-tarball matrix jobs complete with zero ERRORs and WARNINGs.
- [ ] Every remaining NOTE is understood, recorded, and acceptable for an initial CRAN submission.
- [ ] Live local, RSQLite, DuckDB native and fallback, dtplyr, and Arrow evidence agrees with the documented backend matrix.
- [ ] A fresh Standards review reports no unresolved repository-standard violations.
- [ ] A fresh Spec review reports no unresolved deviations from #23 and the accepted ADRs.
- [ ] A fresh Docs & Tests audit reports no broken references, unsupported claims, optional-dependency failures, or critical untested contracts.
- [ ] Any new substantive finding is resolved or moved into a newly approved blocking ticket; this issue is not closed while such a blocker remains open.
- [ ] The final review record gives a clear ready/not-ready verdict without performing the CRAN upload.

## Blocked by

GitHub's native issue dependencies are the authority; this list mirrors them so
the blockers are readable without leaving the ticket.

Every open issue is in 0.1.0, so this list is now the whole remaining backlog
rather than a selection from it.

**Open — `ready-for-agent`**

- #65 — `cran-comments.md` still describes an earlier tree
- #144 — a `NULL` option value is rejected where `.key` and `.id` document `NULL` as "use the default"
- #184 — a zero-column dtplyr input gains a fabricated row in the union expansion
- #185 — the optional-backend table holds every guarded Suggest, and two entries are not backends
- #193 — two modules write out the same tidyselect subscript-chain walk

**Open — `ready-for-human`**

Each carries a brief naming the decision that blocks it; once that decision is
recorded on the ticket, the implementation can be handed to an agent.

- #122 — a factor level equal to `.margin_label` is silently duplicated and reordered on every lazy backend
- #141 — a warning from a user summary expression is repeated once per grouping set, with internal names in its context (absorbs #108)
- #150 — `review-dispositions.md` cites test files and titles that no longer resolve
- #159 — the `Unknown `.by` column` branch is unreachable from the public interface
- #169 — a helper taking bare column names rejects an injected quosure, naming a fault the caller does not have

**Closed**

- #39
- #98 — native grouping-sets adapter omits result-name guards
- #99 — `duckdb()` writes to the user's home filespace
- #100 — untyped base-R errors from static expression analysis
- #101 — `$` field names misread as data-mask references
- #102 — `compute()` fails on lazy SQL backends when `.sort` is set
- #103 — renaming selections build a plan naming a nonexistent column
- #130 — share reads in a call head bypass the dependency guard, silently
title: Run the final CRAN-readiness review

body:
Git updates now supply each target worktree's R Review-ready entry, supervisor, and evidence implementation, replacing the separately synchronized launcher in #1114 / ADR 0039. Pinned local main owns accepted registration and outer supervision; a candidate cannot authorize its own limited execution.

The runner preserves cumulative Full/Documentation/Repository obligations, original execution provenance, authenticated promotion, and existing package/artifact gates. Request-owned storage, seven-day retirement, and atomic key renewal preserve active/recovery state and negative-observation vetoes. Environment identities include actual Git/Python implementations, Python cached bytecode, and refusal of unregistered startup modules. Unreadable directories and nonregular files are rejected before they can become incomplete inventories or blocking streams. Development dependencies are declared separately from package runtime Imports.

Quarto admission checks required render/Pandoc/Deno features and private storage compatibility. Compatible versions and cache layouts are accepted; actual versions, contents, and configuration remain evidence inputs. Validation starts with empty private caches after metadata preparation; authorized retries retain those caches. CI continues following stable Quarto and its bundled Pandoc.

Linux process fixtures use a dedicated account and retain strict production process inspection. Runtime-input fixtures hold unrelated tools fixed and control positive Python cache startup, while the negative case still loads and rejects an actual external startup module. This removes hosted-runner tool visibility and system sitecustomize assumptions without relaxing production admission.

Validation at `9fda5c57b3b23acdc620de1551eea6b7ecb6c570`: normal installed-CLI Full request `e1bdd527035c41acadbf47377db1549a` passed with terminal exit 0, confirmed cleanup, 188/188 files, four observed workers, 0 ERROR / 0 WARNING / 0 NOTE. All inherited regression and replacement native/renderer contracts passed; both source linters and committed CI artifact contracts passed. Current Linux lint, document/site/PostgreSQL and all five R-CMD-check environments pass; the release matrix also passes, and only the optional PR coverage measurement is still running. The two-axis follow-up confirms S1/F1/F2 resolved and no new findings in either axis; the review record is https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/pull/1117#issuecomment-6557260032 . Validation records map 37 evidence cases, 70 admission cases, 194 baseline shared-gate calls and 19 inherited registrations, including the runtime inventory follow-up. Earlier f8 results and canceled subsequent trials remain historical snapshots.

This is the bootstrap implementation. The accepted installed CLI remains required until reviewed code is adopted into local main, old requests are drained, and migration publishes protocol-4 delivery. Real new-R Full/Documentation/Repository executions and cross-clone reuse remain rollout acceptance work. Legacy results are not new-R execution origins. Operational acceptance for issue #1114 remains outstanding.
title: Run Review-ready from the target worktree with R

body:
## Goal

Add one safe, non-mutating local command centered on:

```sh
Rscript tools/cran-preflight.R
```

The command must reduce CRAN rejection risk by checking the actual source tarball that would be submitted, while preserving the existing separation between local checks, GitHub Actions, remote services, semantic review, and human release work. It is a release gate, not a general package-quality dashboard and not a release automation command.

## Context

At commit [`6dbe351`](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/tree/6dbe3510f70b165cfcacd18306f17c256c82a0bd), marginplyr is version `0.1.0`, `Config/marginplyr/cran-status` is `unpublished`, `NEWS.md` calls this the initial CRAN submission, and [`cran-comments.md`](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/blob/6dbe3510f70b165cfcacd18306f17c256c82a0bd/cran-comments.md) records the expected `New submission` NOTE. There is no `LinkingTo` field. The package has eight Imports and these Suggests:

- optional execution backends or input paths: `arrow`, `duckdb`, `dtplyr`, `data.table`, and `RSQLite`;
- `DBI`, which is directly used but is also present through `dbplyr`'s hard-dependency closure and therefore cannot be proven absent by the depends-only job;
- documentation, test, and example dependencies: `knitr`, `quartabs`, `quarto`, `spelling`, `testthat`, `tibble`, and `tidyr`.

The optional-dependency contract is already unusually strong and must remain single-sourced in [`optional_suggest_spec()`](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/blob/6dbe3510f70b165cfcacd18306f17c256c82a0bd/tests/testthat/helper-optional-backends.R). All optional execution paths go through the version-aware guard in [`inst/suggests/guard.R`](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/blob/6dbe3510f70b165cfcacd18306f17c256c82a0bd/inst/suggests/guard.R). The current release matrix:

- builds one source tarball and checks that artifact rather than the checkout;
- runs release, devel, and oldrel checks;
- runs a real `_R_CHECK_DEPENDS_ONLY_=true` job with isolated libraries;
- runs one live job per optional backend, with the other backends genuinely absent;
- proves structurally that every test executes in at least one single-backend configuration;
- runs checktor against the same tarball on `workflow_dispatch`.

Routine [`R-CMD-check.yaml`](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/blob/6dbe3510f70b165cfcacd18306f17c256c82a0bd/.github/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml) remains the full-Suggests development matrix. [`lint.yaml`](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/blob/6dbe3510f70b165cfcacd18306f17c256c82a0bd/.github/workflows/lint.yaml) already owns Jarl plus package-aware lintr; documentation regeneration, site verification, and coverage have separate workflows. A current R-hub v2 workflow also exists.

Issue #40 performed a one-time final readiness review, and PR #503 added the current Jarl/checktor release gates. This issue does not repeat either task: it defines the durable one-command local gate and the release-stage contract around it.

### Current finding to preserve, not fix here

The latest checks for `6dbe351` are not all green: [R-CMD-check run 34182486941](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/actions/runs/34182486941) and [release-matrix run 34182486493](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/actions/runs/34182486493) failed while reading the Bioconductor 3.23 annotation `PACKAGES` index during the unstated-dependency check. The immediately preceding checks for `38da450` passed. Treat this as an external/infrastructure failure that must be rerun and resolved before release, not as a WARNING to allowlist and not as scope for this implementation.

## Research findings

### CRAN and R guidance

- CRAN asks maintainers to submit a source package produced by `R CMD build` and run `R CMD check --as-cran` on the tarball intended for upload, preferably using current R-devel. Warnings and significant notes must be eliminated or explained.
- Suggested packages must be used conditionally. A real no-Suggests check needs both an isolated library and `_R_CHECK_DEPENDS_ONLY_=true`; `_R_CHECK_FORCE_SUGGESTS_=false` alone does not hide packages that are already installed.
- CRAN checks portability, user/global state, writes outside temporary or package-owned locations, check time, use of at most two cores, and graceful handling of unavailable external resources.
- The CRAN submission checklist and Cookbook identify metadata, examples, return documentation, `\dontrun{}`, references, software/package naming, authorship, and licensing as reviewer-sensitive areas. Several require semantic judgment rather than regex-based failure rules.
- CRAN URL checks are network-sensitive. Permanent redirects and reproducible broken URLs are actionable; DNS/timeouts/rate limits need a bounded retry and must be reported as unavailable rather than silently passed.

### r-lib release workflow

- `usethis::use_release_issue()` is useful as the outer human lifecycle checklist. It covers preparation, remote checks, reverse dependencies, comments, versioning, submission, and follow-up; the local command should be one checkbox inside it.
- `rcmdcheck` can check an existing source tarball and returns structured errors, warnings, and notes. Use it with `build_args = NULL`; do not ask it to rebuild the checkout.
- The current `r-lib/actions` standard workflow is routine multi-platform CI, not a final gate: by default it omits the PDF manual, disables incoming checks, installs Suggests, and does not fail on every NOTE.
- The `r-lib/actions` no-Suggests example installs hard dependencies only, but marginplyr's existing isolated depends-only and per-backend jobs are stronger. Do not add a second generic no-Suggests workflow.

### R-hub and win-builder

- `rhub::check_for_cran()` is deprecated and defunct. R-hub v2 uses `rhub_setup()`, a committed workflow, `rhub_doctor()`, and `rhub_check()` against a pushed branch.
- R-hub is supplementary and is not maintained by CRAN. Use a targeted platform that covers a residual risk; do not run every platform or repeat marginplyr's stronger no-Suggests CI.
- win-builder remains distinct because CRAN states that its Windows-devel check uses the same infrastructure as CRAN's Windows checks. It accepts a source tarball and returns results asynchronously.

### Requested precedents

- ThinkR's [`prepare-for-cran`](https://github.com/ThinkR-open/prepare-for-cran/tree/ec5bc0614ce6e0b489f19de3b8e27c865cda14ef) is a useful category inventory, but it mixes mutation, repeated tests/examples/checks, coverage, remote submission, versioning, and release. Adopt its risk categories, not its script structure.
- Davis Vaughan's [`extrachecks`](https://github.com/DavisVaughan/extrachecks/blob/a37e1ee87e47e99ba0ed88a4dfe417141ca5d89e/README.md) is useful first-hand reviewer/rejection history. Presence of generated `\value{}` sections, an inventory of examples/`\dontrun{}`, URL status, and no-Suggests execution can be checked mechanically; usefulness of examples, justification of `\dontrun{}`, description quality, references, wording, and authorship/licensing truth require semantic review.
- ThinkR [`attachment`](https://github.com/ThinkR-open/attachment/tree/8e73618c051c394d5dbe094129eb1065821dbf3d) cannot infer marginplyr's dependency intent. Its location rule would promote guarded `arrow::`, `data.table::`, and `DBI::` calls in `R/` to Imports, while its Rmd/Qmd scan misses conditionally defined vignette dependencies. Its test scan also sees package names in fixtures. `att_from_namespace()` can document/clean by default, and `att_amend_desc()` rewrites `DESCRIPTION`. It is unsuitable as either a blocking dependency classifier or an automatic final-gate mutation.
- Posit's current [`cran-extrachecks` skill](https://github.com/posit-dev/skills/blob/b58a92e7c479b7795f4f003490b046c01e345fce/r-lib/cran-extrachecks/SKILL.md) is useful as a semantic checklist, but its heuristic preferences do not outrank CRAN primary sources or marginplyr's repository contracts. In particular, it must not replace marginplyr's version-aware optional guard or unpublished-installation policy.

### Other tools

- Keep Jarl and lintr in their existing blocking lint workflow; do not rerun them inside local preflight.
- Use `spelling` in local preflight because the current spelling test skips under CRAN semantics and there is no equivalent blocking release-stage spelling result. The existing `inst/WORDLIST` provides the reviewed vocabulary.
- Let CRAN incoming URL checks run normally. Use `urlchecker::url_check()` only as a targeted read-only retry/diagnostic when check output reports a URL problem; never call `url_update()`.
- Do not add `checkhelper`: its user-space audit reruns tests, examples, a full check, and vignette builds, and still does not prove arbitrary user state is untouched.
- Do not add `pkgcheck`: it targets rOpenSci review, duplicates check/coverage/general-quality tools, and adds unrelated system dependencies.
- Keep `covr` in the existing coverage workflow, outside the CRAN gate. CRAN has no general coverage threshold.
- Do not reconsider or add `goodpractice`.

## Decisions

1. **The actual source tarball is the local authority.** Build from a disposable archive of a clean `HEAD`, then pass that exact `.tar.gz` to `rcmdcheck` with `build_args = NULL` and `--as-cran`. Do not use `--no-manual`. Explicitly enable CRAN incoming remote checks for this final local command.
2. **The command is non-mutating.** It must not document, render committed sources, amend dependencies, update URLs, install packages, edit `cran-comments.md`, bump a version, create a release issue, dispatch remote checks, submit, or release.
3. **There is one local release mode.** Do not add `default`, `deep`, `quick`, or other assurance levels. Diagnostic/output-path switches may change retention or verbosity, never the pass criteria.
4. **All ERRORs and WARNINGs block. Unknown NOTEs block.** The only initial allowlist entry is the normalized incoming-feasibility NOTE whose sole finding is `New submission`, and only while `Config/marginplyr/cran-status` is `unpublished`. It remains visible and must be explained in `cran-comments.md`. Do not carry `Days since last update` into the final release allowlist.
5. **Network failure is not success.** A reproducible 4xx/broken URL or permanent redirect is a package failure. DNS, timeout, rate-limit, and 5xx results that remain after one bounded retry are infrastructure/unavailable failures and still block completion without being labeled as package defects.
6. **Do not use attachment.** Dependency assurance comes from `R CMD check`, marginplyr's existing dependency registration/tests, the isolated depends-only job, and live per-backend jobs. A human grep-based dependency-intent audit remains required when dependency metadata changes, as already documented in `AGENTS.md`.
7. **No-Suggests remains CI-owned.** Do not reproduce isolated libraries locally. The existing depends-only job plus per-backend matrix is the authoritative evidence; do not add the generic r-lib/actions no-Suggests example or R-hub `nosuggests` to the default path.
8. **Jarl/lintr, documentation regeneration, site checks, and coverage remain in their current CI owners.** The release checklist requires those workflows to be green for the candidate SHA; the local command does not rerun them.
9. **Remote checks are explicit later stages.** The local command prints them as pending but never dispatches them. R-hub v2 checks a pushed SHA; win-builder checks the exact retained tarball.
10. **Semantic review runs once the candidate is frozen and deterministic local/CI checks are green, before remote checks.** Any later metadata, documentation, example, dependency, or executable-source change invalidates it.
11. **`usethis::use_release_issue()` remains the human orchestrator.** It is run separately at the beginning of release preparation, and records candidate identity and evidence from every stage.
12. **Use the same architecture for first and update submissions.** Submission-type data changes the allowlist and human checklist, not the command's assurance level.
13. **Do not add a new ADR.** This is an operational release contract, not a package-domain/API decision. Keep the executable contract beside `tools/cran-preflight.R`, keep CI-specific rationale in workflow/script headers, and link this issue from those owners. Do not duplicate the full rationale in always-loaded context.

## Proposed architecture

```text
clean release-candidate commit
        |
        +--> local preflight
        |      disposable archive -> one source tarball
        |      spelling + checktor + full --as-cran/manual/incoming
        |      strict result classification + retained evidence bundle
        |
        +--> CI for the same SHA
        |      routine full-Suggests OS/R matrix
        |      docs/lint/site/coverage owners
        |      one-tarball release/devel/oldrel matrix
        |      exact depends-only + live optional-backend jobs
        |
        +--> semantic CRAN review
        |      cited, non-mutating agent review; human dispositions
        |
        +--> remote checks
        |      targeted R-hub v2 pushed-SHA check
        |      exact-tarball win-builder R-devel check
        |
        +--> human release issue
               cran-comments, evidence links, update-only revdeps,
               version/submission/approval/publication follow-up
```

Evidence is valid only for the recorded commit. Any later tracked change invalidates local, CI, semantic, and remote evidence and restarts the sequence.

## Local preflight specification

### Preconditions and candidate identity

`tools/cran-preflight.R` must:

1. run only from the marginplyr repository root;
2. refuse a dirty tracked/index/untracked-nonignored worktree before doing expensive work;
3. record `HEAD`, package/version, `Config/marginplyr/cran-status`, R version/platform, Quarto, Pandoc, TeX/manual prerequisites, and relevant checker versions;
4. verify that every declared Suggest required for the full-Suggests check is installed at its declared minimum version, and fail as unavailable rather than install anything;
5. create a disposable source tree from the clean commit (for example with `git archive HEAD`), never by modifying the checkout;
6. build exactly one source package with `R CMD build` in that disposable area;
7. verify the tarball package/version against `DESCRIPTION`, calculate SHA-256, and use this same file for every tarball-based local check.

The implementation must add `^tools$` to `.Rbuildignore`, so the release driver itself is not shipped.

Declare preflight-only R packages in `Config/Needs/preflight` rather than Imports/Suggests. This field should cover `checktor` (at the version owned by the existing baseline), `rcmdcheck`, and `urlchecker`; `spelling` remains a package Suggest because its test is shipped. The command checks these prerequisites and prints a separate installation hint, but never installs them. It reports the local R version rather than querying and mutating toward a newer R; the human release issue confirms that it is current release/R-patched, and the same-SHA release matrix supplies mandatory R-devel evidence.

### Required checks, once each

Run these required checks without separately rerunning tests or examples:

1. `spelling::spell_check_package()` against the unpacked candidate tarball, with `vignettes = TRUE` and the shipped `inst/WORDLIST`. Any unrecognized word blocks; preflight does not update the wordlist.
2. the existing checktor wrapper against the candidate tarball. Unexpected findings and stale baseline rows both block. Preserve its report. Its reviewed baseline is independent of the R CMD check NOTE allowlist.
3. `rcmdcheck::rcmdcheck()` against the candidate tarball with `build_args = NULL`, `args = "--as-cran"`, full Suggests, PDF manual, vignette rebuild, and CRAN incoming remote checks enabled. Capture every ERROR, WARNING, and NOTE; do not use rcmdcheck's hidden/inconsequential-note configuration.
4. if and only if the CRAN check reports a URL problem, run one bounded read-only `urlchecker::url_check()` retry against the unpacked candidate after a short delay, preserve both observations, and classify the result under the network policy above. Do not run a second unconditional URL scan.
5. verify the repository status is byte-for-byte the same status record as before the run. Any candidate-tree mutation is a tool failure even when checks otherwise pass.

The check itself already executes examples, tests, and vignettes. Do not also call `devtools::test()`, `testthat::test_dir()`, `devtools::run_examples()`, `devtools::build_vignettes()`, checkhelper's umbrella audits, or coverage.

### NOTE and `cran-comments.md` policy

Centralize NOTE classification in one helper used by local preflight and `.github/scripts/check-tarball.R`; do not maintain two lists.

Each allowlist entry must have:

- an anchored normalized signature;
- applicable submission state;
- a rationale;
- a required `cran-comments.md` explanation marker;
- regression fixtures for match, near-miss, and wrong-state cases.

For the initial implementation, permit only a CRAN incoming-feasibility NOTE containing the maintainer line and `New submission`, with no additional incoming finding, while CRAN status is `unpublished`. Do not require the NOTE to appear because incoming services can vary. Report it as `ALLOWED NOTE`, never suppress it. Any additional line/finding makes it unknown and blocking.

Require `cran-comments.md` to exist. Its leading `N errors | N warnings | N notes` counts must match the full local check, and every allowed NOTE must have its required explanation marker. Mismatch blocks and is fixed outside preflight.

Routine push/PR CI may continue to annotate unknown R-devel NOTEs without failing. A manual `workflow_dispatch` release-matrix run must use strict release classification and fail on every unknown NOTE. Remove `Days since last update` from strict release acceptance; a rapid resubmission is a human CRAN-comments decision, not a permanent automatic exemption.

### Safety, artifacts, and output

- Do not call any mutator or installer. Specifically prohibit `roxygen2::roxygenise()`, README rendering, `attachment::att_amend_desc()`, `attachment::att_from_namespace()` with documentation enabled, `urlchecker::url_update()`, `usethis::use_release_issue()`, version helpers, remote dispatch, submission, and release helpers.
- Put disposable source/build/check directories outside the repository.
- Retain a small evidence bundle outside the repository for both success and failure: candidate tarball, SHA-256 manifest, machine-readable step results, human-readable summary, full check log/directory, checktor report, and conditional URL diagnostic. Print its absolute path.
- A retention/output option may choose a different external directory, but cannot change checks or pass criteria.
- Summary rows must show at least `passed`, `failed`, `allowed-note`, `unavailable`, or `skipped`, elapsed time, and evidence path. Required checks may not be silently skipped; non-applicable conditional diagnostics are the only normal skip.
- The final summary must show candidate SHA, tarball name/hash, ERROR/WARNING/NOTE counts and classifications, tool versions, worktree before/after status, and the still-pending CI/semantic/remote/human stages.

Exit codes:

- `0`: every required local check passed, all notes are allowed, no required service is unavailable, `cran-comments.md` matches, and the worktree is unchanged;
- `1`: candidate/release-policy failure (including ERROR, WARNING, unknown NOTE, spelling/checktor failure, actionable URL, or comments mismatch);
- `2`: invocation, prerequisite, tooling, or infrastructure failure (including inconclusive required network checks); this also blocks release but distinguishes the candidate from the environment;
- `130`: interrupted.

## CI specification

Do not add another broad workflow.

- Keep `R-CMD-check.yaml` as routine full-Suggests multi-platform development CI.
- Keep `lint.yaml`, `document.yaml`, altdoc/site verification, and coverage in their current owners. The human release issue requires them to be green at the candidate SHA; local preflight does not duplicate them.
- Keep `release-matrix.yaml`'s one-tarball build, release/devel/oldrel jobs, `depends-only`, structure proof, and generated live backend jobs. These are the authoritative no-Suggests/optional-backend checks.
- Keep checktor manual-only in the release matrix for independent CI evidence and an uploaded report. Local checktor gives immediate feedback; the manual job proves the same reviewed rule set in a clean runner against the matrix tarball. Both must share the checker/baseline, not fork implementations.
- Refactor NOTE classification so a manual release-matrix dispatch is strict, while normal push/PR runs retain their low-noise annotation behavior.
- Do not replace marginplyr's no-Suggests architecture with `r-lib/actions`' generic example, and do not add R-hub `nosuggests` to the normal release path.

The human release issue must record successful workflow URLs for the exact candidate SHA. A transient dependency-index failure is rerun and recorded; it is never converted into a warning exemption.

## Remote check specification

Remote checks occur only after local preflight, all required CI at the pushed SHA, and semantic review are green/dispositioned.

### R-hub v2

- Use the existing R-hub v2 workflow and current `rhub::rhub_check()`; never use `rhub::check_for_cran()`.
- Select one current R-devel Linux container on a non-Ubuntu distribution to cover a residual OS/R environment not already in the GitHub matrix. At the research date this is `atlas`; resolve by capability from current `rhub_platforms()` rather than silently accepting a renamed/stale alias. Fall back to the current Ubuntu-clang R-devel container only if no such image exists.
- Do not run compiled-code sanitizers, LTO, valgrind, `rchk`, or every OS for this pure-R package without a new concrete risk.
- Do not run R-hub `nosuggests` by default because the existing CI evidence is stronger.
- Record commit SHA, resolved platform/image, date, and result URL in the release issue.

### win-builder

- Upload the exact tarball retained by local preflight, verifying its SHA-256 first.
- Run Windows R-devel at minimum. Add release/oldrelease only if a Windows-specific change or missing CI coverage creates a concrete residual risk.
- Record tarball hash, environment, date, and result in the release issue.

Neither service is launched by `tools/cran-preflight.R`. They require pushed/external state, are asynchronous, and should not turn a local read-only command into an external-action command.

## Semantic review specification

After the candidate is frozen and local/CI deterministic gates pass, run a non-mutating agent review using the current Posit `cran-extrachecks` skill as a checklist, with CRAN primary sources and repository policy taking precedence. Record the skill commit/version and candidate SHA.

Review:

- whether `Title` and `Description` are informative, non-circular, non-promotional, and follow CRAN naming conventions;
- whether exported examples are meaningful, runnable, and representative, not merely present;
- every `\dontrun{}`/`\donttest{}` use and its justification;
- whether implemented methods/algorithms need a reference and whether citations are well formed;
- software/package names, acronyms, URLs, and reviewer-sensitive wording;
- `Authors@R`, `cph`, license/copyright facts, and bundled-license consistency;
- user state, filesystem, external-resource, and parallelism risks that deterministic tools cannot establish completely;
- `cran-comments.md`, unpublished installation instructions, and optional-backend explanations against marginplyr's own contracts.

Each finding must cite a candidate location and either an authoritative source or label itself as a heuristic. Concrete policy contradictions, missing required content, and reproducible defects block the human release checklist. Style preferences and uncertain reviewer taste are advisory, but every advisory needs an explicit accept/fix disposition. The review never edits the candidate.

Repeat semantic review only after a change to `DESCRIPTION`, `NAMESPACE`, `R/`, `man/` sources, examples, vignettes, README, NEWS, licensing, dependencies/guards, or `cran-comments.md`; otherwise retain it for the same SHA.

## Dependency audit specification

Do not add attachment or a replacement static dependency classifier.

- `R CMD check` owns mechanically detectable undeclared namespace/dependency usage.
- `optional_suggest_spec()` remains the single repository registry for guarded Suggests and generated backend jobs.
- The exact isolated depends-only CI job owns “does the package load, test, run examples, and build vignettes without optional packages?”
- Live backend jobs own “does each backend execute when the others are really absent?”
- Existing suite-coverage and isolation verifiers prevent false-green skip/install states.
- When `DESCRIPTION`, dependency calls, or optional guards change, the implementation/release PR performs the manual `pkg::` and bare-name audit already required by `AGENTS.md`, including dependency-closure inspection with `packageDescription()` where relevant.
- `DBI` remains a declared direct Suggest even though `dbplyr` currently installs it transitively; no-Suggests evidence must not claim that DBI was absent.
- “Possibly unused dependency” remains a review finding, not an automatic failure or warning generated by an incomplete scanner.

Why no attachment API:

- `att_amend_desc()` mutates and can rewrite a correct optional split incorrectly;
- `att_from_namespace()` is not read-only by default;
- read-only AST inventory still cannot distinguish a guarded runtime Suggest from an Import;
- Qmd/test/fixture behavior produces both false negatives and false positives in this repository;
- adding attachment solely for this audit would add maintenance cost without authoritative signal.

## Human release checklist

Use `usethis::use_release_issue()` separately and add/retain project-specific checkboxes for:

- frozen candidate SHA and clean worktree;
- local preflight summary and tarball SHA-256;
- all required CI URLs for that SHA, including exact depends-only/backend evidence;
- semantic review link and every advisory disposition;
- R-hub and win-builder evidence;
- `cran-comments.md` consistency and explanation of every allowed remote/local NOTE;
- initial-submission metadata/install-link review while CRAN status is `unpublished`;
- for future updates: current CRAN results, reverse-dependency checks, downstream communication if needed, and the update rationale;
- versioning, submission, confirmation email, publication, and post-publication changes as distinct human actions.

Do not call `use_release_issue()` from preflight. It creates external state and belongs at release-planning time, not candidate inspection time.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `Rscript tools/cran-preflight.R` is the single local release-gate command and has one invariant assurance level.
- [ ] It refuses a dirty candidate before expensive work and leaves the repository status unchanged on success, candidate failure, tool failure, and interruption.
- [ ] It builds from a disposable copy of clean `HEAD`, produces exactly one source tarball, records SHA-256, and passes that exact file to every tarball-based local checker.
- [ ] It runs `R CMD check --as-cran` through structured `rcmdcheck` without rebuilding, without `--no-manual`, with full Suggests, Quarto/vignette rebuild, PDF manual, and CRAN incoming remote checks.
- [ ] It does not separately rerun tests, examples, vignettes, coverage, Jarl, lintr, documentation generation, or site generation.
- [ ] Shipped spelling is blocking; a conditional URL retry distinguishes actionable failure from unavailable infrastructure and never edits URLs.
- [ ] Every ERROR and WARNING blocks. Unknown NOTE blocks. The state-scoped `New submission` NOTE is visible, narrowly matched, explained, and tested against near misses. `Days since last update` is not a strict-release allowlist entry.
- [ ] `cran-comments.md` check counts and allowed-note markers are verified without editing the file.
- [ ] The checktor baseline/report remains the owner of deterministic extra findings; unexpected and stale rows block.
- [ ] Exit codes `0`, `1`, `2`, and `130` follow this specification and are covered by subprocess-level tests or fixtures that do not require a full CRAN check for every branch.
- [ ] The summary and machine-readable result contain candidate identity, tool versions, step status/duration, check counts, note classification, tarball hash, evidence path, worktree invariant, and pending external stages.
- [ ] Final artifacts are retained outside the repository; `tools/` is excluded from the package tarball.
- [ ] Preflight-only packages are declared in `Config/Needs/preflight`, not promoted to Imports/Suggests, and missing tools produce an installation hint plus exit `2` without installation.
- [ ] No code path installs/updates packages, documents/renders committed sources, updates dependency fields/URLs/comments, dispatches remote checks, changes versions, submits, or releases.
- [ ] Local preflight and `.github/scripts/check-tarball.R` share one NOTE classifier and regression fixtures; manual release-matrix runs fail on unknown NOTEs while routine push/PR runs remain low-noise.
- [ ] Existing isolated depends-only, suite-coverage, library-isolation, and live backend jobs remain the authoritative optional-dependency evidence; no duplicate generic no-Suggests job is added.
- [ ] No dependency on `attachment`, `checkhelper`, `pkgcheck`, `covr`, or `goodpractice` is added for preflight.
- [ ] Release documentation/checklist names the exact sequence: local -> CI -> semantic -> targeted R-hub + exact-tarball win-builder -> human submission actions, including initial/update differences.
- [ ] Automated tests cover clean/dirty state, mutation detection, prerequisite/unavailable classification, tarball identity, NOTE matching and near misses, comments mismatch, result summary, and command failure propagation using stubs/fixtures where full external checks would be slow or flaky.
- [ ] The implementation PR runs the repository-mandated context, Jarl, package-aware lintr, documentation, test, and relevant release-matrix checks, and records the candidate SHA for all hosted evidence.

## Out of scope

- Fixing any current CRAN readiness finding, including the transient current CI failure.
- Submitting to CRAN, changing the package version/status, editing `cran-comments.md`, or updating installation instructions.
- Reworking package code, tests, examples, vignettes, metadata, optional-backend guards, or dependency classification.
- Replacing the existing CI matrices, adding a general package-quality score, or adding coverage thresholds.
- Automatic reverse-dependency checks inside local preflight; they are an update-only human/CI release stage.
- Automatic remote dispatch, release creation, GitHub issue creation, version bumping, or publication follow-up.
- Encoding subjective CRAN reviewer taste as blocking regex rules.

## Risks / open questions

No design question blocks implementation.

Residual risks are handled by policy rather than left to implementation discretion:

- CRAN NOTE text and remote service/platform names can change. Unknown output fails closed; fixtures and source links make the small policy surface easy to update deliberately.
- Network services can be transient. The command separates infrastructure (`2`) from candidate failures (`1`) but neither is a pass.
- The semantic skill contains community heuristics. Reviewers must label heuristic findings and apply the stated evidence hierarchy.
- The current checktor baseline has reviewed findings. Unexpected and stale entries remain blocking, and this issue does not silently reinterpret the baseline.
